questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The reputation of the University and the course list. And that there were courses in english

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The administration and Abroad-team was very helpful at Freie, though it seems weird that they have not a generalized way of receiving students at each department of the uni. And in general, there are so many documents that need to be filled out, both from Erasmus and the uni, which makes it a lot of work to gather all information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: assistance pr mail primarily. An online info meeting as well. And of cource the introductory days, which made a lot of things clearer as all informations were difficult to find online.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it through a facebook group. It was surprisingly easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed it because I didn't seek to obtain a new social network. Probably it is nice living on a campus housing if you are looking for new friends or a social place to stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As I didn't make use of student housing I don't know

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This was very difficult and impossible to find before the orientation days. I am used to register for courses a long time before starting, and it was really challenging to just wait and hope that I could get registered at the courses I wished for. Also I decided to take courses on different departments than my own (political science) and until just before the start of classes i did not know which courses I was able to follow, because it was up the single professor to accept me at their course. It seems like there must be a better way to do this

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Through a website called Campus Management which generally wasn't very intuitive. And the courses I have followed (fx on sociology or anthropology) I wasn't able to register for these in Campus Management and here I just need to rely on the individual professor to sign my registrations/attendance documents.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Mail-contact with the incoming team. They were helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful overall and got the classes I wanted. But this took a lot of time, and only until I showed up at the classes I knew whether I was accepted or not.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Being VERY patient and knowing that you are able to design your own stay to a high degree at Freie University if you are contacting each professor.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Almost 5. As I was able to follow courses on other departments, I had a really good and relevant academic program. The only reason I did not choose 5 on the scale above is because I had a teacher who was simply not able to teach his course in english even though it was offered in english.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style was in some ways different. At my host uni they expected much more participation which is both "more work" but also really nice and a better way to teach/learn. We had to read less pages at each class compared to my home uni, but this was only nice because then we were able to actually discuss the texts in dept. The teaching style reminded me a bit of high school but in a good way (more student participation - less lecture style)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 1. Ecosocial Movements and Pedagogies of Resistance, 2. Deconstructing Eurocentrism: Gender, Knowledge, Power, 3. Emotions and Social Stratifications, 4. Debt, Guilt, and Social Subjugation, 5. The Anthropology of Class

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them were very interesting and well organized. The course of Debt, Guilt and .... had a great syllabus but the teaching was not working very well unfortunately, as the professor was not sufficiently fluent in English and also cancelled several times (only an hour in advance) due to health reasons i think.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: >there were a lot of nice sports activities etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: o

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. The only thing i wished was available was language courses that was less intensive. I chose not to follow german on beginner's level as the only way I could follow this class was participating 8 hours a week plus homework and this sounded like too much for me while also studying full time. I wish I could have had german lessons once a week - this would also make my adjustment to the local culture better.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated that there is a bigger diversity both in Berlin but definitely also at the campus of Freie. I had courses where we were from everywhere around the world and that was a really nice and special learning environment.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Being patient with the registration for courses in the beginning of the stay. 2. That the exams are during august/september, so you wont get any holiday (almost) if you choose the summer semester. 3. You are expected to participate more in classes than at UCPH

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I have read and discussed many exciting and interesting things. The academic outcome has been the most rewarding to me.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That I have to write a lot of exams during what I normally perceive as my summer holiday.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
